sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on GRIN2B-related disorders
We are writing to the GRIN2B Foundation, a parent-run organisation for this community, and would welcome the views of CureGRIN Foundation.
The Rare Epilepsy Network and DEE-P Connections also connect with this community, the latter through a partnership signal rather than a formal membership record.
Published work links GRIN2B-related disorders to both gain of function and loss of function, so the mechanism differs between variants.
Simons Searchlight and the GRIN Variant Patient Registry include people with these disorders, and the Simons Searchlight online study is recruiting.
A registry and a survey study of epilepsy-dyskinesia syndromes are recruiting.
Two phase 3 studies in GRIN-related neurodevelopmental disorders, Beeline and TAP-GRIN, are recruiting.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on GRIN2B-related disorders, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
